notes.claim: In a basis of eigenvectors, a matrix just scales each basis arrow by its eigenvalue, so applying it 100 times scales each by the 100th power of its eigenvalue.
A matrix can be diagonalised when it has n linearly independent eigenvectors; a shear does not have enough eigenvectors to span all of space.

For i6: symmetrical components, used for unbalanced three-phase faults, rest on the Fortescue transformation, which diagonalises a matrix with circular symmetry; its parts are the positive, negative and zero sequences.

sources.title: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues | 3Blue1Brown
sources.quote: Since all one of these matrices does is scale each basis vector by some eigenvalue, applying that matrix, say, 100 times will just correspond to scaling each basis vector by the 100th power of the corresponding eigenvalue

sources.title: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues | 3Blue1Brown
sources.quote: A shear, for example, doesn't have enough eigenvectors to span all of space
An n × n matrix with repeated eigenvalues can be diagonalized provided we can obtain n linearly independent eigenvectors

sources.title: 100 Years of Symmetrical Components | MDPI
sources.quote: The fundamental property that has ensured the great success of the Fortescue transformation in electrical engineering studies is the diagonalisation of a matrix with circular symmetry
